status.en: 8 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 60% more than the week before, most of them in Tigray, Amhara and Oromo.
status.nb: 8 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 60 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i Tigray, Amhara og Oromo.

summary.en: Ethiopia has intensified its regional role by offering to host a comprehensive Sudanese dialogue and Abiy Ahmed is urging Sudanese parties to join a mediation table, while drone strikes linked to Ethiopia killed four people and damaged a United Nations building in Khartoum. At the same time, artillery shelling by Ethiopian forces in Alamata killed 14 civilians, prompting Amnesty International to call for a war crimes investigation in Tigray. Leaked intelligence suggests coordination between Eritrean and Sudanese actors in drone strikes on Mekelle and Assosa. Ethiopian forces have regained control of border areas near Badme, and clashes continue along the Afar-Somali border over territory, drought and resources. 2,824 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Etiopia har styrket sin regionale rolle ved å tilby å være vert for en omfattende sudansk dialog, og Abiy Ahmed oppfordrer sudanske parter til å delta i et meklingstabell, mens droneangrep knyttet til Etiopia drepte fire personer og skadet en bygning til FN i Khartoum. Samtidig drepte artilleriskudd fra etiopiske styrker i Alamata 14 sivile, noe som fikk Amnesty International til å kreve en etterforskning av krigsforbrytelser i Tigray. Leaket etterretning tyder på koordinering mellom eritreiske og sudanske aktører i droneangrep mot Mekelle og Assosa. Etiopiske styrker har gjenvunnet kontrollen over grenseområder nær Badme, og kamper fortsetter langs den afarske somaliske grensen om territorium, tørke og ressurser. 2 824 drepte i kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency or Amhara war is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
